title: Investigate & fix tenant-blend caused by proxy service token forwarding
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Summary: Several customers reported spiky invoice corrections after a new internal proxy service (req-proxy) was introduced for sidecar integrations. We observed that when req-proxy forwards upstream requests using ephemeral forwarding tokens, usage attribution sometimes records the downstream workspace (proxy host) instead of the originating tenant workspace. This causes underbilling of the true tenant and overbilling of the proxy owner, and it affects quota enforcement and per-tenant rate limiting.

Scope: multi-tenant attribution correctness when requests traverse internal proxy/sidecar services that mint or forward ephemeral tokens. Includes attribution at meter ingestion, rate-limiter ownership, and quota counter assignment.

Why this matters: Inaccurate billing attribution breaks trust with customers, can cause incorrect quota throttles, and may lead to revenue leakage. The pattern is reproducible under moderate concurrency and when token-forwarding headers are present alongside service identity headers.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a test tenant A and a proxy-hosted tenant B (owner of req-proxy).
2) Configure req-proxy to accept Tenant-A-origin requests and forward them upstream using a forwarded-token header (X-Forwarded-API-Key) and include X-Service-Id for proxy identity.
3) Send burst of 200 concurrent generation requests through req-proxy with trace IDs and distinct tenant A request IDs.
4) Observe meter ingestion logs in metering pipeline: check attributed_tenant field on events and compare to the original tenant in request metadata.
5) Confirm quota counters and rate-limiter metrics for tenant A show lower usage while proxy host shows inflated usage.
impact_summary: Several production customers experienced incorrect billing rows and unexpected quota rejections. Preliminary audits show ~0.4% of last-30d token traffic was misattributed for orgs using the proxy pattern; estimated revenue impact: medium but customer trust impact high. This also causes noisy alerts in customer observability dashboards and increased support tickets.
root_cause_analysis: Root cause appears to be a precedence bug in attribution logic: when the ingestion service sees both a forwarded-token header and a service-identity header, it prioritizes the token presented (which may be an ephemeral forwarding token issued by the proxy) without validating original-tenant claims in the X-Original-Tenant or trace metadata. Additionally, the token exchange flow sometimes uses a short-lived token that is minted under the proxy's service account for upstream communication, so the token subject maps to proxy owner. There's insufficient validation that the original tenant identity is carried and authorized to be billed for the forwarded token.
proposed_solution:
1) Update the attribution pipeline to prefer explicit original-tenant headers (X-Original-Tenant, X-Requester-Workspace) when present and cryptographically verifiable (signed trace or request context).
2) Require token exchange flows to include an optional 'delegation_claim' that binds the forwarded token to the original tenant id; treat tokens without delegation_claim as proxy-owned.
3) Add an ingestion-time validation step: if a forwarded-token is present, consult the token introspection service to verify delegation_claim and map attribution accordingly.
4) Emit a new audit log event when attribution chooses proxy-owner due to missing delegation_claim so we can retroactively reconcile.
5) Add end-to-end integration tests and a chaos test that simulates concurrency through the proxy.
acceptance_criteria: Attribution pipeline preferrs verifiable X-Original-Tenant header over raw token subject when delegation_claim exists.
Token introspection returns delegation_claim mapping used to set attributed_tenant in >99.99% of test runs under concurrency.
No regression in latency SLOs for ingestion service (p50/p95 p50+<3ms added, p95+<15ms added).
Backfill script created to reconcile misattributed events for affected window and generate corrected billing rows for export.
New audit logs exist and are searchable in Splunk/Datadog for all forwarded-token decisions.
Security review signoff completed for delegation_claim handling.
technical_tasks: Add delegation_claim parsing to token-introspection service and update token schema.
Change ingestion pipeline attribution logic to check X-Original-Tenant and delegation_claim before falling back to token subject.
Create integration test harness that deploys req-proxy with forwarding behavior and validates attribution correctness under 500 concurrent flows.
Implement reconciliation job that identifies misattributed events (date range) and writes corrected usage rows to billing queue.
Instrument audit events and dashboards for forwarded-token attribution decisions.
Prepare migration/rollout plan and feature flag in ingestion service for gradual rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable feature flag for ingestion in us-west-2 on 2 low-traffic clusters for 48 hours. Monitor attribution divergence, latency, and audit logs. Phase 2: expand to all ingestion replicas; run reconciliation job for last 30 days of misattribution. Phase 3: disable legacy fallback unless delegation_claim explicitly absent for backward compatibility (announce deprecation).
backfill_notes: Reconciliation job will: 1) query raw metering events for date range 2026-02-01 to 2026-03-01 where proxy_host shows non-null and forwarded-token header present; 2) introspect tokens to recover delegation_claim where possible; 3) generate corrected usage rows and place them in billing corrections queue with source=reconciliation and tag ENG-33011; 4) create audit CSV for finance team. Expect job runtime ~2h for 30-day window on billing cluster.
security_considerations: Delegation_claim handling must be validated by security. The token introspection endpoint requires strict auth and rate limiting. Avoid storing raw API key material in logs; only store token fingerprints and delegation_claim subject. Coordinate with Security to perform threat modeling and add unit tests for claim validation.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add a Datadog monitor that triggers if daily misattribution rate >0.01% of token traffic or if audit events showing 'proxy-owner chosen' spike by >3x baseline. Add dashboard tiles: attributed_tenant distribution, forwarded-token rate, reconciliation progress.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Verma: Initial triage complete. Found correlation between req-proxy rollout (2026-02-18) and onset of misattribution. Captured sample logs and traced a replayable session.
2026-03-03 - Luca Moretti: Implementing token-introspection changes. Early patch adds delegation_claim extraction but behind feature flag.
2026-03-05 - Priya Das: Security kickoff scheduled for 2026-03-07. Need to ensure delegation_claim format prevents tampering.
2026-03-08 - Omar Singh: Finance requested a prioritized backfill for Feb-20..Mar-08 due to a billing dispute opened by a top-tier customer.
2026-03-10 - Tomas Eriksen: Canary infra ready in us-west-2. Ingestion replicas will be toggled by feature flag at 10% initially.

2026-03-12 - Luca Moretti: Deployed canary with delegation_claim checks enabled on two clusters. Initial results: misattribution rate dropped from 0.42% to 0.006% on canary traffic. No significant latency increase observed (p95 +8ms).
next_steps: Complete security review, run reconciliation for priority customer window, widen canary to 50% if no regressions for 48 hours, then schedule full rollout. Document proxy integration requirements and publish a developer guide for delegation_claim usage.
